//: ESLINT-ONLY project, split out 2026-08-06 when client/tsconfig.json (the
typecheck:client CI gate) was scoped down to a ratchet of currently
closure-clean files. eslint.config.js's type-aware block for
client/test/**/*.ts and client/js/**/*.d.ts needs `parserOptions.project`
to point at a tsconfig whose `include` actually contains the files being
linted, or typescript-eslint fails outright with 'file was not found in
any of the provided project(s)'. That's a real constraint, not a style
choice: type-aware ESLint rules ask the TypeScript language service for
semantic info about the file being linted, and the language service only
knows about files reachable from some project's `include`.
This is safe to keep broad (the same include client/tsconfig.json used to
have, before the ratchet): the TS language service that backs ESLint's
typed rules resolves type info per file and tolerates OTHER files in the
program having errors — it does not require the whole program to compile
cleanly, and nothing here runs `tsc --noEmit` against this file as a gate
(see package.json: only client/tsconfig.json is wired to typecheck:client).
If it ever *is* wired to a `tsc --noEmit` gate, it will fail loudly (client
still has 1174 outstanding errors on this wider file set) — do not add
this file to any CI step without first re-running the ratchet math in
client/tsconfig.json's own comment block.
Keep this file's compilerOptions and include in sync with what
client/tsconfig.json used to declare pre-ratchet; do not let it drift into
being a second, competing source of truth for what 'the client project' is.
